docs.text: Agentic PharmacoGX Contributors: Nasim Bondar-Sahebi, Nikta Feizi, Michael Tran, Omar Ibrahim Contact: nasim.bondarsahebi@uhn.ca Overview Agentic PharmacoGx is a model-agnostic framework for reproducible pharmacogenomic analysis through natural-language queries. Integrating PharmacoGx and curated datasets from ORCESTRA , the framework enables AI agents to execute established computational methods through reusable skills and tools, ensuring results are computed rather than inferred by language models. Set Up Prerequisites Pixi is required to run this project. If you haven't installed it yet, follow these instructions Installation Clone this repository to your local machine Navigate to the project directory Set up the environment using Pixi: pixi install Documentation Click here to view the full documentation.

docs.text: Agent setup The agent is Biomni with a local model ( qwen3:8b ) run by Ollama . Everything is installed with pixi . Requirements pixi : installs Python, Biomni and Ollama. R with PharmacoGx : included by pixi on Linux; on macOS, install it yourself. About 6 GB of free disk space for the model, and an internet connection for the first run. A GPU is optional; it makes the agent much faster. Install git clone https://github.com/bhklab/agentic-pharmacogx.git cd agentic-pharmacogx pixi install Run pixi run agent-example Q014 # one question (test) pixi run agent-example Q014 --skills # one question, with our skills pixi run agent # all questions pixi run agent --skills # all questions, with our skills Replace Q014 with any question ID (Q001–Q100). To see the prompt without running the agent, add --dry-run . The first run starts Ollama and downloads the model (about 5 GB) automatically. The agent downloads the data it needs from ORCESTRA itself. Answers are saved in data/results/benchmark/agent/ and the agent's step-by-step log in logs/benchmark/ . Notes Skills are in skills/ . With --skills , the agent gets all of them. Model: set once in pixi.toml ( AGENT_MODEL ). Repeats: every run saves to a new folder, so running it again makes a new run.

docs.text: Benchmark Can an agent answer pharmacogenomic questions as well as an expert using PharmacoGx? We answer 100 questions twice, once manually with PharmacoGx (the reference) and once by the agent , and measure how often the answers agree. 100 questions + 12 PSets │ ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐ ▼ ▼ MANUAL AGENT PharmacoGx code in R question in plain English │ │ └─────────────┬─────────────┘ ▼ COMPARE % agreement How it works Manual answers: answer each question with PharmacoGx, using the PSet versions listed below. This is done once. Agent answers: send each question to the agent in a new session. The agent uses the PSets in data/procdata/psets/ . Repeat as often as needed. Compare: score each agent run against the manual answers. Files metadata/ ├── benchmark_questions.csv the 100 questions ├── benchmark_prompt_template.txt prompt for one test question (agent downloads PSets) └── benchmark_prompt_template_local.txt prompt for the full run (agent uses PSets in data/procdata/psets/) workflow/ ├── scripts/benchmark/ │ ├── manual/ manual answers (PharmacoGx in R) │ │ ├── manual.R all 100 questions │ │ └── manual_tier1-3.R one script per tier │ └── agent/ agent answers (see Agent setup) │ ├── agent_example.py one question │ ├── agent.py all questions │ ├── live_log.py writes each step to the log │ └── run_one.sh, run_agent.sh run on the lab server └── notebooks/benchmark/ └── compare.Rmd comparison and figures data/ not in git ├── procdata/psets/ PSets downloaded from ORCESTRA └── results/benchmark/ all results Design Same data as the manual answers: in the full run the agent uses the PSets already in data/procdata/psets/ and does not download anything. PharmacoGx only: the manual answers use PharmacoGx functions, not custom code. Blind: the agent never sees the manual answers. Independent: each question runs in a new agent session. Same format: both sides answer as qid | answer | method . Runs A run is the agent answering all 100 questions once. Each run is saved in its own folder, with its settings (agent, model, parameters) recorded automatically. Runs can be added at any time: repeat a run to test reproducibility; change the model or agent to test an improvement. Scoring An answer is correct if it matches the manual answer in data, endpoint, method and result (within tolerance). We report % agreement per tier and overall, with 95% confidence intervals, and how consistent the results are across runs. Questions The 100 questions get harder in three tiers: Tier 1 – Data retrieval (Q001–Q020): find cell lines, drugs and measurements. Tier 2 – One PharmacoGx function (Q021–Q050): pick and run the right function. Tier 3 – Multi-step analysis (Q051–Q100): combine several functions to answer a question. Datasets The questions use 12 PharmacoSets (PSets) from ORCESTRA , a platform for curated pharmacogenomic datasets. The manual answers use the latest version of each PSet, listed below with a link to its dataset record. PSet ORCESTRA name Dataset Questions CCLE CCLE_2019 10.5281/zenodo.18759113 29 CTRPv2 CTRPv2.1_2016 10.5281/zenodo.21794049 18 GDSC2 GDSC_2020(v2-8.2) 10.5281/zenodo.5787145 15 gCSI gCSI_2019 10.5281/zenodo.7829857 8 NCI_ALMANAC NCI_ALMANAC 10.5281/zenodo.23920676 8 GDSC2_matrix GDSC²_Matrix 10.5281/zenodo.23921019 7 NCI60 NCI60_2026 10.5281/zenodo.21043047 3 HMCL HMCL 10.5281/zenodo.23920418 3 PRISM PRISM_2020 10.5281/zenodo.7826864 3 GDSC-SQUARE Anchor GDSC²_Anchor 10.5281/zenodo.23921232 2 GRAY GRAY_2017 10.5281/zenodo.7826847 1 GDSC1 GDSC_2020(v1-8.2) 10.5281/zenodo.7829915 1 To see all PSets on ORCESTRA from R: PharmacoGx::availablePSets() . A further 21 questions use all 12 PSets.

docs.text: Data Sources Overview This section should document all data sources used in your project. Proper documentation ensures reproducibility and helps others understand your research methodology. How to Document Your Data For each data source, include the following information: 1. External Data Sources Name : Official name of the dataset Version/Date : Version number or access date URL : Link to the data source Access Method : How the data was obtained (direct download, API, etc.) Access Date : When the data was accessed/retrieved Data Format : Format of the data (FASTQ, DICOM, CSV, etc.) Citation : Proper academic citation if applicable License : Usage restrictions and attribution requirements Example: ## TCGA RNA-Seq Data - **Name**: The Cancer Genome Atlas RNA-Seq Data - **Version**: Data release 28.0 - March 2021 - **URL**: https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/ - **Access Method**: GDC Data Transfer Tool - **Access Date**: 2021-03-15 - **Citation**: The Cancer Genome Atlas Network. (2012). Comprehensive molecular portraits of human breast tumours. Nature, 490(7418), 61-70. - **License**: [NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy](https://sharing.nih.gov/genomic-data-sharing-policy) 2. Internal/Generated Data Name : Descriptive name of the dataset Creation Date : When the data was generated Creation Method : Brief description of how the data was created Input Data : What source data was used Processing Scripts : References to scripts/Github Repo used to generate this data Example: ## Processed RNA-Seq Data - **Name**: Processed RNA-Seq Data for TCGA-BRCA - **Creation Date**: 2021-04-01 - **Creation Method**: Processed using kallisto and DESeq2 - **Input Data**: FASTQ Data obtained from the SRA database - **Processing Scripts**: [GitHub Repo](https://github.com/tcga-brca-rnaseq) 3. Data Dictionary For complex datasets, include a data dictionary that explains: Column Name Data Type Description Units Possible Values patient_id string Unique patient identifier N/A TCGA-XX-XXXX format age integer Patient age at diagnosis years 18-100 expression float Gene expression value TPM Any positive value Best Practices Store raw data in data/rawdata/ and never modify it Store processed data in data/procdata/ and all code used to generate it should be in workflow/scripts/ Document all processing steps Track data provenance (where data came from and how it was modified) Respect data usage agreements and licenses! This is especially important for data that should not be shared publicly

docs.text: Developer Notes Purpose of This Section This section is for documenting technical decisions, challenges, and solutions encountered during your project. These notes are valuable for: Future you (who will forget why certain decisions were made) Collaborators who join the project later People coming from your publication who want to reproduce your work Anyone who might want to extend your research What to Document Design Decisions Document important decisions about your project's architecture, algorithms, or methodologies: ## Choice of RNA-Seq Analysis Pipeline [2025-04-25] We chose the kallisto over STAR pipeline for the following reasons: 1. The CCLE dataset is very large, and kallisto is faster for quantifying large datasets 2. GDSC used kallisto, so we can compare our results with theirs Technical Challenges Record significant problems you encountered and how you solved them ## Sample Name Format Issue [2025-04-25] We encountered a problem with sample name formats between the CCLE and GDSC datasets. The CCLE dataset uses "BRCA-XX-XXXX" format, while the GDSC dataset uses "BRCA-XX-XXXX-XX". We had to write a script to remove the last two characters from the sample names in the GDSC dataset. Dependencies and Environment Document specific version requirements or compatibility issues: ## Critical Version Dependencies [2025-04-25] SimpleITK 2.4.1 introduced a bug that flips images, so we froze version 2.4.0 Best Practices Date your entries when appropriate Link to relevant code files or external resources Include small code snippets when helpful Note alternatives you considered and why they were rejected Document failed approaches to prevent others from repeating mistakes Update notes when major changes are made to the approach

docs.text: Usage Guide Install Everything (Python, Biomni, Ollama, and R with PharmacoGx on Linux) is installed with pixi . pixi pins every version in pixi.lock , so each computer gets the same setup. git clone https://github.com/bhklab/agentic-pharmacogx.git cd agentic-pharmacogx pixi install On macOS, install R and PharmacoGx yourself (pixi provides them on Linux only). Ask the agent pixi run agent-example Q014 --dry-run # show the prompt only, no agent pixi run agent-example Q014 # one question, no skills pixi run agent-example Q014 --skills # one question, with the skills in skills/ pixi run agent # all 100 questions, no skills pixi run agent --skills # all 100 questions, with skills Replace Q014 with any question ID (Q001–Q100). The model is set by AGENT_MODEL in pixi.toml . Each full run saves to a new folder, so running it again adds a repeat. The agent needs a free GPU. If another model is using most of the GPU memory, it runs on the CPU and is very slow. Check with nvidia-smi before a long run. On the lab server, use bash workflow/scripts/benchmark/agent/run_one.sh Q014 --skills . More details: Agent Setup . Manual answers The reference answers are computed with PharmacoGx in R: Rscript workflow/scripts/benchmark/manual/manual.R # all 100 questions Rscript workflow/scripts/benchmark/manual/manual_tier1.R # or one tier at a time (tier1, tier2, tier3) Each question has its own block with notes on what was done and any problem found. The notes at the end of manual.R list the problems and the questions they affect. Where things are saved What Where Questions metadata/benchmark_questions.csv Prompt template metadata/benchmark_prompt_template.txt Skills skills/ PSets from ORCESTRA data/procdata/psets/ Agent answers data/results/benchmark/agent/ Agent step-by-step logs logs/benchmark/ Manual answers data/results/benchmark/manual/answers.csv (+ figures/ ) How the benchmark is designed and scored: Benchmark .
